investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T20:42–20:50Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule a new remote-agent pod. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two eligible peer-pod nodes are at capacity and preemption cannot free any slots. The pod remained unscheduled for 126–146 seconds across all three checks, which caused the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) to time out before it could collect any evidence, producing a complete contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both peer-pod nodes have no remaining VM slots and preemption found no victims, so no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled until capacity is freed or expanded.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not match the pod's node selector, meaning the schedulable node pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

Tertiary — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all available VM slots: if other remote-agent pods are running and not being cleaned up, they may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocations that the eval pod needs.

Lower confidence — eval cleanup not releasing VM resources: if a prior eval run's withCleanup path failed to delete a remote-agent pod, its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocation would persist and reduce available capacity for subsequent runs.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is not exhausted on the two eligible nodes, the scheduler message would be misleading and another cause (e.g., a quota policy or admission webhook) would need investigation.

If the two peer-pod nodes show zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable (i.e., the resource is not configured at all), the root cause would be a node configuration regression rather than capacity exhaustion.
If the pod's node affinity/selector was recently changed to exclude previously eligible nodes, the 4-node mismatch would be the primary cause rather than VM slot exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes.

If no pods are currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on the two eligible nodes, the resource accounting may be incorrect (e.g., leaked allocations from terminated pods not yet garbage-collected).

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting before the eligible pool shrinks to zero.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as a structured evidence field (e.g., schedulerMessage, unschedulableReason) so future failures produce richer contract evidence even when the pod never starts.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted on Production Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-08 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the required kata.peerpods.io/vm pod because 2 nodes reported insufficient kata peer-pod VM capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or pool limit reached), and 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure in the production Kubernetes cluster that hosts the Swarm-backed remote agent runtime. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not proceed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract validation to fail completely. This is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure condition; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage independently.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: the peer-pod VM quota or the underlying cloud VM pool backing those nodes is at capacity, preventing any new remote agent pods from being scheduled. This is the most directly supported cause given the 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message across all three checks.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata peer-pod capable nodes), and those 2 are already at VM capacity. If the affinity configuration changed or nodes were removed/relabeled, the eligible pool would shrink to zero effective capacity.

Cluster node count or peer-pod node pool under-provisioned: only 2 of 6 nodes are configured to support kata.peerpods.io/vm workloads. If concurrent eval runs or production workloads consumed all available VM slots on those 2 nodes simultaneously, new pods would be unschedulable until slots are freed.

Transient resource spike or concurrent workload contention: a burst of remote agent creation requests (from other eval runs, CI pipelines, or production traffic) may have temporarily exhausted the peer-pod VM slots, causing this run's pods to queue and eventually fail.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-08T20:42–20:50Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The production Kubernetes cluster has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity to schedule a new remote-agent pod. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two eligible peer-pod nodes are at capacity and preemption cannot free any slots. The pod remained unscheduled for 126–146 seconds across all three checks, which caused the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) to time out before it could collect any evidence, producing a complete contract gap (evidence: expected-output.missing-required-evidence). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: both peer-pod nodes have no remaining VM slots and preemption found no victims, so no new remote-agent pod can be scheduled until capacity is freed or expanded.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes do not carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource or do not match the pod's node selector, meaning the schedulable node pool is effectively limited to 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size.

Tertiary — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all available VM slots: if other remote-agent pods are running and not being cleaned up, they may be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocations that the eval pod needs.

Lower confidence — eval cleanup not releasing VM resources: if a prior eval run's withCleanup path failed to delete a remote-agent pod, its kata.peerpods.io/vm allocation would persist and reduce available capacity for subsequent runs.

Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not proceed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and causing the expected-output contract validation to fail completely. A passing result for remote-agent-create while remote-agent-state still fails would localize the problem to the state-polling step specifically rather than the shared scheduling layer.

Confirmation that the node affinity/selector on the remote agent pod spec was recently changed (and now excludes the kata-capable nodes) would shift the root cause from capacity exhaustion to a misconfiguration.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocks Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval pod remained unscheduled for 146 seconds before the check timed out, producing zero evidence output and failing every required-evidence assertion.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are ineligible due to node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to help (no lower-priority victims found), every eval attempt that requires provisioning a remote agent pod fails immediately at the scheduling layer — before any application code runs. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion localized to the remote-agents kata peer-pod node pool, not a code defect and not a user-traffic incident (no traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId, meaning pod scheduling is the very first infrastructure operation — any scheduling failure aborts the entire probe before evidence can be collected.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a previous eval run left VM slots occupied, leaving zero capacity for new probe pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's affinity rules, meaning the schedulable pool is permanently constrained to only 2 nodes regardless of overall cluster size. If those 2 nodes are at capacity, scheduling always fails.

Tertiary — a leaked or stuck remote-agent pod from a prior eval run is holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and was not cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper (source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1916), reducing available capacity for subsequent runs.
Lower confidence — the node pool for kata peer-pods may be under-provisioned for the current eval concurrency, meaning the resource limit is structurally too low rather than transiently exhausted.

affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message directly names kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 nodes that carry this resource class. All three remote-agents checks fail at this layer before any application code executes.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the 2 kata-eligible Kubernetes nodes immediately to determine current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity versus consumed capacity. If slots are fully consumed, identify which pods are holding them.

Search the cluster namespace for any leaked or stuck remote-agent eval pods that may not have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs. Terminate any orphaned pods to free VM slots.

If the node pool is structurally under-provisioned (i.e., the VM slot limit is too low for the eval concurrency), increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the existing 2 nodes or add additional kata-capable nodes to the pool.

Verify that the node affinity and selector rules on the remote-agent pod spec are correct and intentional. If the 4-node exclusion is unintentional, correcting the affinity rules would expand the schedulable pool and reduce pressure on the 2 kata-eligible nodes.

Review the withCleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure it reliably releases kata.peerpods.io/vm slots even when a probe times out or throws an unhandled error, to prevent future slot leakage.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (source-context features.json:185), so this check alone does not trigger a formal outage classification. However, remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183-184), and their simultaneous failure with the same message means the remote-agents feature is at or near its outageAfterFailures=2 threshold.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the 2 kata-eligible nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is available and not fully consumed, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the affinity/selector mismatch or a scheduler bug would need to be investigated instead.

If a subsequent eval run succeeds and returns all 5 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) without any infrastructure changes, the failure was transient (e.g., a briefly occupied slot freed up) rather than a persistent exhaustion.

If the 4 non-matching nodes are found to have kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity but are excluded by an incorrect or recently changed node affinity rule, the root cause shifts to a node selector/affinity misconfiguration rather than capacity exhaustion.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the failure (i.e., the resource shows as available but scheduling still fails), the issue may be a Kubernetes resource quota, admission webhook, or scheduler plugin misconfiguration rather than actual VM slot exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all eligible nodes before attempting remote agent provisioning, and emits a warning if available slots fall below a minimum threshold.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that scans the remote-agents namespace for pods in Running or Pending state that have exceeded their expected lifetime, alerting before they exhaust the VM slot pool.
Add a node-pool health eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote-agent pod's affinity and selector rules, catching affinity drift before it reduces the schedulable pool to zero.

Consider adding a scheduler-timeout-specific evidence key (e.g., schedulerError) to the remote-agent-create and remote-agent-runtime probes so that scheduling failures are distinguishable from application-layer failures in the eval output, enabling faster triage.
